body.statement: Uniformly over sequences in the predictable class satisfying propensity-path stability, the primitive oracle gap, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(\bigl|\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)-\rho_{nm}\bigr|=O_P(b_{nm})\) and the observed discrepancy satisfies \(\bigl|\widehat\rho_{nm}-\rho_{nm}\bigr|=O_P(b_{nm})\). Therefore \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)=O_P(b_{nm})\) if and only if \(\rho_{nm}=O_P(b_{nm})\), if and only if \(\widehat\rho_{nm}=O_P(b_{nm})\). Thus \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\) is an observable rate certificate: tightness of \(\widehat\rho_{nm}/b_{nm}\) certifies frontier-rate validity, whereas \(\widehat\rho_{nm}/b_{nm}\to\infty\) certifies its failure.
body.justification: The theorem turns the latent total-drift boundary into an observed comparison of two fitted row spaces.
body.gap: Khan and Ugander's scalar affine normalizer does not provide an observed spectral diagnostic for a row-fraction SVD.
body.consumer: A data steward can compare the two reported fits and decide whether discarding saved personalization probabilities preserves the rowwise frontier.
